question.problem: Consider the lamina that occupies the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{{y}^{3}},\,0\le y\le 1\}.$ Given that the area of the lamina is $\frac{2}{5}$ square units, find the $y$-coordinate of its centroid.
question.worked_solution:
The centroid of a lamina $D$ with area ${A}_{D}$ is given by $({x}_{c},{y}_{c}),$ where

$$
{x}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\,\text{d}A,\,{y}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Therefore, the $y$-coordinate of the centroid is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{c} & =\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{{y}^{3}}}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}y{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{{y}^{3}}}\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}y[x]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{{y}^{3}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \sqrt{{y}^{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{5/2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{[\frac{2{y}^{7/2}}{7}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{2}{7} \\  & =\frac{5}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
